desc:
A network has n machines numbered 0 to n - 1 and starts with no cables at all. The cables are then installed one by one, in the order given by edges; the entry [u, v] connects machines u and v with a two-way cable.

A cluster is a maximal group of machines that can reach each other through cables (directly or through other machines). Return an array of length edges.length whose k-th element is the number of clusters right after the k-th cable has been installed.

n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[0,2],[3,4],[2,3]]

result = [4,3,3,2,1]

The third cable joins machines that are already in the same cluster, so the count stays at 3.
constraints: edges[k] = [u, v] with 0 ≤ u, v < n and u ≠ v
The same pair of machines may be cabled more than once
hints: Recounting the clusters from scratch after every cable costs O(n + k) each time. Can you update the count instead of recomputing it?
Start with n clusters. A new cable either joins two different clusters (count goes down by one) or lies inside a cluster (count unchanged).
Keep a union-find structure. For each edge find the roots of both ends: if they differ, union them and decrement the counter; always append the counter to the answer.
editorial: Begin with n singleton clusters, which is the count before any cable exists. A union-find (disjoint-set) structure answers the only question that matters: are the two endpoints of the new cable already in the same cluster? If their roots differ the cable merges two clusters, so we union them and subtract one from the counter. If the roots are equal the cable is redundant for connectivity and the counter does not move.

Append the counter after processing each edge. With path compression every find is nearly constant time, so the total is about O((n + k) · α(n)) for k cables. Note the answers never increase, since adding a cable can only merge clusters.
